clue.text: Point weapon? That's harsh!

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass
a trident is a three-pronged spear

explanation.surface: Someone asked to aim a sharp weapon protests at how severe the order is.
explanation.definitionFit: A strident voice or tone is loud and grating, which is a harsh sound.

clue.text: Aware of what's happening? No

parts.note: the answer read as wordplay says the word on has its letters switched, which gives this word

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether another is alert and gets a flat 'No'.
explanation.definitionFit: Switched on is an informal term for being alert and well informed.

clue.text: With Ruby Green, consider what you might want to do in the bedroom?

definitions.text: what you might want to do in the bedroom?

parts.note: ruby is a shade of red
eco- describes green, environmental concerns
to rate is to consider or judge

explanation.surface: A saucy suggestion about colour schemes and what happens in the bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at something racy; the definition is merely doing up the room.
explanation.definitionFit: To redecorate a room is to paint or paper it afresh, a typical bedroom makeover.

clue.text: That's good! Scoundrel's given up second home

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means read from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: ah is an exclamation of satisfaction
a cad is a man who behaves dishonourably

explanation.surface: A cheer as a rogue is forced to surrender his country retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacha is a Russian country house, typically a holiday home kept besides a city flat.

clue.text: Writings by Donne about very ordinary people

indicators.note: by means beside, so the two pieces sit next to each other
about means moved around, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: scripts are pieces of writing

explanation.surface: Works by the poet John Donne about everyday folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but it rearranges DONNE to NONDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nondescripts are people lacking distinctive features, so dull and unremarkable.

clue.text: Mats in work for prayer, supposedly

indicators.note: to work something is to knead or shape it, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Prayer mats are being made, presumably for worshippers to kneel on.
explanation.walkthrough: MATINS is the tempting anagram, but matins is a service, not a prayer; the insect called the praying mantis holds its forelegs as if praying, hence 'supposedly'.
explanation.definitionFit: The praying mantis takes its name from its folded forelegs, so it is a 'prayer' only by appearance.

clue.text: Turned away — one nurse in particular upset

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: the nurse goes in, inside the other piece
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: a particular, as a noun, is a detail
EN is an enrolled nurse

explanation.surface: One nurse in particular was upset and turned away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'particular' is a noun here, a detail, not an adjective qualifying the nurse; EN is a British enrolled nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: Alienated means estranged, made hostile or distant, so turned away from others.

clue.text: Accept bet son refused

indicators.note: the son is refused, turned away, so his letter is removed

parts.note: a stake is a sum wagered
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A wager is accepted but the son was turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: To take an offer is to receive it willingly, which is what accept means.

clue.text: See 22
Late in the year, briefly attending hospital department — it's dirty

indicators.note: attending means accompanying, so one piece sits beside the other

parts.note: in December, shortened to IN DEC
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A late-year hospital appointment is described as filthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecent material is obscene, which is what a dirty joke or picture is called.

clue.text: Former party leaders taken into custody

parts.note: with 'leaders', the phrase names two former British party leaders; the first is Nick Clegg, ex-leader of the Liberal Democrats
the second former leader is Ed Miliband, ex-leader of the Labour Party

explanation.surface: Ex-leaders of political parties have been arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: Two first names make the answer: Nick Clegg led the Liberal Democrats and Ed Miliband led Labour, both British parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicked is British slang for arrested by the police.

clue.text: Not working at that point with my department (unofficially)

parts.note: off means not functioning, switched off
there means at that place
cor is an exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'

explanation.surface: An off-duty remark at a meeting with someone's department, kept unofficial.
explanation.definitionFit: Off the record is an idiom for remarks not to be quoted or made officially.

clue.text: Rosette's a frivolity? Don't listen!

parts.note: a cockade is a rosette or knot of ribbons worn on a hat
fun is light-hearted amusement

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a rosette is just a bit of nonsense, then tells the listener to ignore it.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces sound like 'cock a deaf 'un', meaning turn a deaf ear: pretend not to hear.
explanation.definitionFit: To cock a deaf 'un is a British idiom for deliberately ignoring what is said.

clue.text: Damn! This is complicated with no guarantee of success

indicators.note: complicated means tangled, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: An exasperated person swears at a fiddly task that may not work.
explanation.definitionFit: Hit-and-miss describes something haphazard, sometimes working and sometimes not.

clue.text: Game that's played on board

parts.note: on board suggests a board game, but it means aboard a ship, on the deck

explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' points to chess or draughts; the game is played aboard ship, on its deck.
explanation.definitionFit: Deck tennis is a ring-throwing game traditionally played by passengers on a ship's deck.

clue.text: Strange nation, English, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, an English person finds the nation odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means weird in an unsettling, uncanny way.

clue.text: Finish off ale in time for relaxation

indicators.note: relaxation loosens the letters, letting them settle in a new order

explanation.surface: Finish your beer in time to relax.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate is to get rid of completely, or kill, which is finishing someone off.

clue.text: Do the job OK but leave little margin for error

definitions.meaning: first meaning: read literally, to cut something finely, doing it well
second meaning: the idiom for allowing only just enough time or room

explanation.walkthrough: The literal phrase describes a neat piece of cutting; the idiom means leaving yourself almost no slack.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut it fine is an idiom for allowing barely enough time or space, while literally it means slicing thinly and well.

clue.text: Over four weeks' money lost at one Riviera resort — precariously placed

indicators.note: the money is lost, so its letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a month is a little over four weeks
I is the Roman numeral one
Nice is a city on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: A gambler has lost more than a month's pay at a Riviera casino and is in a shaky position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' takes M from MONTH to leave ONTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on thin ice is an idiom for being in a risky position where one slip brings disaster.

clue.text: Finally had row (was fond of the bottle)

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the next word

parts.note: a rank is a row, as of soldiers or taxis

explanation.surface: Someone finally had an argument, the bracket noting they were a drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' wants to be a quarrel; here it is a line, as in a taxi rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who drank, in the sense of drinking habitually, was fond of alcohol.

clue.text: Had listened to jockey here?

indicators.note: to jockey is to jostle and manoeuvre, so these letters are pushed around into a new order

explanation.surface: A question about where a rider sits to hear instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads loosely as a whole: a jockey is 'here', on the horse; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider sits on the seat strapped to a horse, so that position is where the jockey is.

clue.text: Bit of hot stuff about to pick up Vlad — help!

indicators.note: the reversed word picks up the setter, taking him inside
about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: lava is molten rock, a bit of very hot stuff
Vlad is the setter, who calls himself I

explanation.surface: A cry for help as an attractive person comes to collect the setter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns LAVA into AVAL, and I, the setter Vlad, goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Avail as a noun means use or benefit, as in 'to no avail', so help.

clue.text: Spotted in the distance — that's cheeky!

indicators.note: spotted in says the letters are found concealed within the words that follow

parts.note: the answer read as an instruction turns its second part round, and that turned part is found across the end of 'the' and the start of 'distance'

explanation.surface: Someone spots something far off and exclaims at its impudence.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: SIDE back gives EDIS, and EDIS sits in thE DIStance.
explanation.definitionFit: A backside has cheeks, the buttocks, so it is the thing that is literally cheeky.

clue.text: Having turned up, go against Harris for now

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: to go is a euphemism for to pee
V is short for versus, against

explanation.surface: Someone who has arrived decides to oppose Harris for the time being.
explanation.walkthrough: Kamala Harris was the US Vice-President when this appeared; veep is US slang for that office.
explanation.definitionFit: Veep is informal American shorthand for vice-president, the post Harris then held.

clue.text: American gym teacher perhaps a distant relative?

parts.note: a physical education instructor, a man who teaches PE

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a US PE teacher could be a far-off member of the family.
explanation.definitionFit: An ape-man, a primitive hominid, is a remote evolutionary relative of humans.

clue.text: The same people present

parts.note: do is short for ditto, meaning the same
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: The same group of people turning up again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like an adjective (here, attending); it is a noun, a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A donation is a gift, which is a present given to a cause.

clue.text: Youngster taking course at Oxford got his head down

indicators.note: the youngster takes the course in, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: a kid is a child
PPE is Philosophy, Politics and Economics, an Oxford degree course

explanation.surface: A young student on an Oxford course got stuck into work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got his head down' suggests studying hard; it means slept. Kip is British slang for sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipped is British slang for slept, and getting your head down is an idiom for going to sleep.

clue.text: Greatly admires PM's astonishingly honest admission about Truss's ultimate direction

indicators.note: the admission goes around the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: 'I do lie' would be an astonishingly frank thing for a Prime Minister to say

indicators.note: ultimate means the last letter of the word

parts.note: S, south, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A dig at a Prime Minister being shockingly candid about Liz Truss's future course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the S from the end of Truss inside I DO LIE, making IDOLISE; another S for south follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To idolise someone is to worship them, admiring them to excess.
